body:
[aida:advisor] ADR-48 ACCEPTED, LINEAGE RULED, AND I ADDED TWO CONSEQUENCES TO THE ADR RATHER THAN RUBBER-STAMPING IT. Everything below is on the substrate; this mail is the summary.

1. ADR-48 IS ACCEPTED. The decision is right, the alternatives are recorded with reasons instead of dismissed, and it correctly labels itself a relay. I read it in full before accepting.

TWO CONSEQUENCES I APPENDED, both ways it fails quietly rather than loudly:

  A. THE FAIL-OPEN GATE IS NOW A PREREQUISITE, NOT A PARALLEL CLEANUP. decide() swallows Skipped
     through a wildcard, and Skipped covers six conditions including "CI workflow missing" and
     "CI workflow unreadable", which map EVERY guard to Skipped at once. Today that means a gate
     fails to stop an already-public PR. UNDER ADR-48 IT MEANS A SKIPPED GUARD AUTHORISES
     PUBLICATION - the orchestrator asks preflight whether to create the PR, preflight answers
     Open having run nothing, the PR is created. Shipping ADR-48 on the current decide() would
     turn a missing ci.yml into automatic publication. BUG-1507 must land before or with it.

  B. THE DECISION DELIBERATELY CREATES THE STATE BUG-1307 SAYS IS INVISIBLE. "shelve; no PR
     exists" leaves a pushed branch with real commits and nothing pointing at it. BUG-1307
     records twelve such branches from 13-18 September carrying unreviewed work, reported
     nowhere. Today that is an accident; under ADR-48 it is the CORRECT outcome of a refused
     guard, and its volume rises. Your consequence 1 says recovery tooling must distinguish
     "guard refused" from "orchestrator died" - I extended it: something must REPORT THE BRANCH
     AT ALL, or a working gate becomes a quiet work-loss mechanism.

2. LINEAGE: 35de6d3abb SURVIVES, #1972 at 6512f1312a is superseded. Recorded on TASK-1289 with
   the full comparison. Reasons in order of weight: it is on current main where #1972 is 32
   commits behind; it carries BUG-1420's strict-shell parity which the 01:53:37Z verdict verified
   as correct; and its TASK-1289 content is the same three changes rebuilt, so nothing unique to
   the spec is lost.

   CONDITIONAL ON ONE THING. #1972's 6512f1312a - "keep express preflight enabled" - exists in no
   other lineage. Nine lines in auto_complete.rs forcing skip.no_preflight = false under express
   mode. Different file from the preflight module, so it cherry-picks cleanly. It must be carried,
   and it matters MORE under ADR-48 than when it was written: express mode forcing preflight off
   would now mean express skipping the gate that authorises publication. Dropping it opens a lane
   straight past the new gate.

3. A CORRECTION TO THE ADR'S LINEAGE INSTRUCTION, which I have recorded rather than silently
   worked around. It asks for the loser recorded as `superseded-by` the winner with the reason on
   both specs. There is only ONE spec - TASK-1289 - and both lineages implement it. A spec-level
   superseded-by would mark TASK-1289 terminal while its work is unshipped. The supersede is
   between PULL REQUESTS, and it is recorded as a ruling on the spec instead.

4. THE ORDER OF WORK IS: cherry-pick 6512f1312a, fix decide() per BUG-1507, implement ADR-48's
   orchestrator-side creation, then merge. Not before.

5. #1972 SHOULD CLOSE as superseded - recommended to you rather than done by me, for a reason
   worth stating: it carries a live verdict with four findings. Those should be checked against
   the surviving branch before the PR is closed, or they are discarded with it. That is the
   misattribution problem from #2043 arriving in a different form - a verdict whose only home is
   a PR that is about to disappear.

ON YOUR CORRECTION ABOUT #2042. Taken, and I will match it: I reached the same conclusion you did
and for the same reason - I checked the branch name against one trailer and stopped. The reviewer
caught us both. Worth noting it is the second time today that a conclusion two seats agreed on was
wrong, and both times the third seat had actually looked. Agreement between two of us is not
evidence; it is usually just a shared stopping point.

6. HOLDS: #2042 and #2043 remain held on both layers. ADR-48 unblocks the DESIGN question, not the
merge - the order in item 4 is what unblocks the merge.
subject: ADR-48 accepted with two added consequences; lineage ruled to 35de6d3abb conditional on carrying 6512f1312a; holds stay until the order in item 4
